newsitem.title: CROATIA: CROATIAN CALL MONEY RATES RISE, LIQUIDITY LOW.
newsitem.headline: CROATIAN CALL MONEY RATES RISE, LIQUIDITY LOW.

text.p: Croatian call money rates were slightly higher on Thursday amid low liquidity and rocketing demand, dealers said.

"The situation is diametrically opposed to that of yesterday. There is a very high demand for funds, and we are some 20 million kuna ($3.1 million) short of matching it. This situation may still be the aftermath of the monthly pension payments," dealer Jasenka Blagaic said.
Fresh deals were put at 47.8 million kuna, most of them call money deals generally made at 7.0 percent but a few also granted at 8.0 and 9.0 percent.
Term loan prices held despite strained liquidity, with one-week interbank funds granted at 12 percent, one-month deals at 13 and 14 percent and three-month money costing 18 percent.
Banks' balances fell to 483 million kuna, the lowest in more than a month and banks had some 16 million kuna in outstanding Lombard loans, up from Wednesday's four million.

Wednesday's overnight trade totalled 10.3 million kuna. Some 2.6 million kuna was sought by one bank to cover its shortfalls and the rest was used to cover mandatory reserves. -- Sandra Kalogjera, Zagreb newsroom +385 1 455 7075 ($ = 6.471 Croatian Kuna)
